### Summary

### Problem

Currently, running an older version of `uv` can silently downgrade the `revision` in `uv.lock` when executing `uv lock`. For example, if `uv.lock` has `revision = 5`, running `uv lock` with a version of `uv` that only supports up to revision 3 will downgrade it to revision 3.

This can cause unnecessary confusion and disruption in collaborative projects where contributors use different versions of `uv`. A lockfile generated by a newer version can be inadvertently downgraded by a contributor using an older version, even when they do not intend to change the lockfile format.

I recently encountered this issue when a PR changed `uv.lock` from revision 5 to revision 3. Before the PR, the lockfile was already using the latest revision. This subsequently caused the following error when running `uv sync --frozen`:

```text
error: Frozen lockfile discovery requires a lockfile with revision 5 or later; run `uv lock` to update it
```

### Proposed solution

When `uv` encounters a lockfile whose revision is higher than the highest revision it supports, it should refuse to overwrite the lockfile and report an error instead of silently downgrading it.

If users explicitly want to overwrite such a lockfile with an older revision, they should be required to pass a `--force` option.

This would help prevent accidental lockfile downgrades, reduce unnecessary changes in pull requests, and make collaboration more reliable when contributors use different versions of `uv`.

### Platform

Windows 11

### Version

0.13.5

_No response_
title: Prevent older uv versions from downgrading the lockfile revision
